t: The largest Andean state before the Incas, ruling about 1,000 km of Peru’s desert coast from its capital, Chan Chan.
Chan Chan’s walled royal compounds held palaces, storerooms and burial platforms; each new king seems to have built his own.
Irrigation, conquest and skilled crafts made it rich; the Incas conquered it around 1470 and took its metalworkers to Cusco.
dyk: Around 1450 about 140 children and 200 young llamas were sacrificed in a single event at Huanchaquito, near Chan Chan, apparently soon after heavy rains and flooding.
ev: Chimú culture takes shape in the Moche valley and building begins at Chan Chan
A massacre at Punta Lobos near Huarmey is linked to Chimú expansion to the south
By tradition, Ñançenpinco conquers the coast from the Saña or Jequetepeque valley south to Santa
Chimor absorbs the Lambayeque valley and moves Sicán metalworkers to Chan Chan
About 140 children and 200 young llamas are sacrificed at Huanchaquito near Chan Chan
Inca forces under Topa Inca Yupanqui conquer Chimor; Minchançaman is taken to Cusco
Chan Chan becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is listed as in danger
